'''Sybilla Beckmann''' is a Josiah Meigs Distinguished Teaching Professor of Mathematics, Emeritus, at the [[University of Georgia]] and a recipient of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] [[Louise Hay Award]].

== Biography==
Sybilla Beckmann received her Sc.B. in Mathematics from [[Brown University]] in 1980<ref name="about"/> and her Ph.D. in Mathematics from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] under the supervision of [[David Harbater]] in 1986.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=23108}}</ref> She taught at [[Yale University]] as a J.W. Gibbs Instructor of Mathematics, before becoming a Josiah Meigs Distinguished Teaching Professor of Mathematics at the University of Georgia.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.math.uga.edu/directory/people/sybilla-beckmann-kazez |website=[[University of Georgia]] |title=Sybilla Beckmann-Kazez |accessdate=October 10, 2022}}</ref> She retired in 2020.<ref name="about">{{cite web |url= https://www.math.uga.edu/directory/people/sybilla-beckmann-kazez |website=Sybilla Beckmann, PhD |title=About Me |accessdate=October 10, 2022}}</ref>

Beckmann's main interests include [[numerical cognition|mathematical cognition]], mathematical education of teachers, and mathematics content for [[pre-Kindergarten]] through Grade 8.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://faculty.franklin.uga.edu/sybilla/content/biography|title=Biography {{!}} Sybilla Beckmann|website=faculty.franklin.uga.edu|access-date=2016-11-05}}</ref>
